reasoning_traces.think:
Stimulus trace \( \tau(t) \) encodes temporal memory of prior inputs through convolution with an exponential decay kernel. Reaction potential \( R(t) \) aggregates these traces linearly, forming a scalar measure of readiness to respond. Molar behavior \( B_M \) emerges as a transformed aggregate of molecular behaviors, enabling coarse-grained modeling. These primitives form a hierarchy where stimulus trace feeds into reaction potential, which then influences molar behavior. Failure modes include divergence in \( R(t) \) due to unbounded weight accumulation or loss of temporal resolution in \( \tau(t) \). Dualities arise in that \( \tau(t) \) can be viewed both as a filter and as a memory kernel. The system exhibits criticality when \( R(t) \) approaches threshold, triggering state transitions in \( B_M \).
